section.title: Where shipping rates come from
section.scenario: A checkout service quotes shipping for each order. The team signs a new carrier about once a month, and each carrier has its own rate rule. Changes to ShippingQuote#cost_cents require checkout recertification; carrier registration and individual rate classes can be updated without it.
section.question: Which piece fits this system better, and which stated fact decides it?
section.piece_a:
class ShippingQuote
  def initialize(carrier)
    @carrier = carrier
  end

  def cost_cents(order)
    case @carrier
    when "ups"   then UpsRate.new.cost_cents(order)
    when "fedex" then FedexRate.new.cost_cents(order)
    else raise KeyError, @carrier
    end
  end
end

answer_key.deciding_fact: Changes to ShippingQuote#cost_cents require checkout recertification; carrier registration and individual rate classes can be updated without it.
answer_key.principle: Open for extension, closed for modification at the quote-calculation method: both pieces add a rate class and edit a carrier list, but B leaves cost_cents unchanged.
answer_key.why_other_fails: A adds each carrier by editing the case statement inside cost_cents, requiring checkout recertification. B changes RATES instead, which the scenario allows without recertification.

answers.complete:
pick:b
The scenario says changes to cost_cents require checkout recertification, while carrier registration and rate classes can change without it. Both pieces need a new rate class and a carrier-list entry. B adds that entry to RATES and leaves cost_cents unchanged; A adds it inside cost_cents and requires recertification. B applies open for extension, closed for modification to the quote-calculation method, not to the whole class.
answers.partial:
pick:b
B is better, because changes to cost_cents require checkout recertification.
answers.miss:
pick:a
A is easier to read because all the carriers are listed in one method and there is no constant to look up, so a new teammate can follow it.

extra_answers.label: vague_correct_pick
extra_answers.answer:
pick:b
B looks cleaner and more professional, and it is the more modern way to write this kind of class.

extra_answers.label: other_pick_sound_reason
extra_answers.answer:
pick:a
The scenario says carriers are added monthly. A adds one branch and a new rate class each time, so the monthly edit stays small and dispatch remains explicit. Both options need their carrier list extended.
